text:
Zara: hi all, new hire here. Onboarding blocked: Docker can't pull base images from our internal registry (10.50.5.10) when I'm on the split-tunnel VPN from my home Windows laptop (Windows 11 + WSL2). When I enable the corporate wifi in office it works. Any Windows/WSL2-specific tips?

Eli (Infra): welcome! WSL2 has a NAT layer which often makes split-tunnel hairpinning worse. Can you paste `route PRINT` output from an admin PowerShell and `wsl -l -v`? Also, which VPN client? WireGuard or the company client?

Zara: i've got the output snippets: `wsl -l -v` shows Ubuntu 22.04 on WSL2. In PowerShell `route PRINT` shows 10.50.0.0 via 100.64.0.1 on Interface 12. Docker Desktop is using the WSL2 backend.

Eli (Infra): that 100.64.x next-hop is CG-NAT from your ISP. For Windows/WSL2 the quick options are: 1) add a host route on Windows so traffic to 10.50.0.0/16 uses the VPN interface: run PowerShell as admin and use `New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 10.50.0.0/16 -InterfaceIndex 23 -NextHop 0.0.0.0` (replace InterfaceIndex with your VPN adapter index from `Get-NetAdapter`). Or older command: `route ADD 10.50.0.0 MASK 255.255.0.0 <vpn-gateway> IF <if_index> -p`. 2) use SSH SOCKS via bastion: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rdw -D 1080 rdw-bastion` and set Docker daemon HTTP_PROXY in Docker Desktop to point at socks5 proxy (Docker Desktop supports proxies). 3) run Docker builds inside the bastion via `ssh -J rdw-bastion -- docker build -t me/myimage - < Dockerfile` if you want no local routing changes.

Sam (DevEx): extra WSL note: after adding Windows routes, restart WSL to pick up the changes: `wsl --shutdown` then restart your distro. Also Docker Desktop sometimes caches DNS; toggle the WSL integration off/on if DNS still fails. If you prefer a script, i can share a tiny helper that detects 100.64.0.0/10 next-hop and prints the `New-NetRoute` example for you.

Zara: i added the persistent route with `route ADD` and restarted WSL. Pulls now work and my onboarding script completed. using the SOCKS hack is useful too when i don't want to touch system routes. thanks!

Eli (Infra): great. we'll add a Windows/WSL section to the new-hire network doc and a small Powershell helper. tagging @Sam to add the helper to the onboarding repo.

Infra Bot: Created ticket INF-711: "New-hire: Windows/WSL2 CG-NAT detection and route helper" assigned to Infra.

Zara: awesome, leaving thread for other Windows folks. thanks all :smile:
